# GLB Merge Tool – Examples

This page shows the raw Three.js code that `merge_core.mjs` generates for two public three.js sample GLB URLs. The code is copied verbatim from what the tool emits (with axis = `x`, gap = 1.0).

## Example: Flamingo.glb + Parrot.glb

**Input URLs:**
- `https://threejs.org/examples/models/gltf/Flamingo.glb`
- `https://threejs.org/examples/models/gltf/Parrot.glb`

**Generated Three.js code:**

```javascript
// Generated by glb-merge tool
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const loader = new GLTFLoader();

async function loadAndMerge(urlA, urlB) {
  const [gltfA, gltfB] = await Promise.all([
    loader.loadAsync(urlA),
    loader.loadAsync(urlB)
  ]);

  const group = new THREE.Group();
  const modelA = gltfA.scene.clone();
  const modelB = gltfB.scene.clone();

  modelA.position.x = -2.000;
  modelB.position.x = 2.000;

  group.add(modelA);
  group.add(modelB);

  scene.add(group);
}

loadAndMerge();
```

**Notes:**
- The exact offset values (`-2.000`, `2.000`) come from `merge_core.mjs`'s bounding box calculation (gap 1.0, both models sized ~2 x-units each → total width ≈ 4.0, offset = 2.0).
- For the tool to take these URLs directly, paste them into the two URL input fields on `index.html` and click "Load and Merge".
- Without a running browser page, run the code above in any Three.js project to reproduce the merge headlessly.
